name: Hyperbrowser

modes.label: Cloud browser session ($0.10 per browser-hour, credits)
modes.note: 100 credits/h at 1 credit = $0.001 = $0.10 per active browser-hour, billed per second; same rate on every plan. Browser vCPU/RAM undisclosed (sizes vcpu/ram null - treat one session as one browser). Session billed from create until stop/timeout (stops automatically on CDP disconnect unless keepAlive). Proxy data $10/GB extra (see extras); Fetch/Scrape/agent steps priced separately.

modes.label: Hyperbrowser Sandbox (Firecracker VM), per vCPU-h + GiB-h
modes.note: Default 2 vCPU / 2048 MiB / 8192 MiB disk; API limits vcpus 1-32, memMiB 512-262144, diskSizeMiB 2048-32768, timeoutMinutes max 1440 ('Maximum sandbox lifetime in minutes, measured from VM start'). Billing granularity and minimum not stated (browser sessions are per second). Custom images built from local Docker images via 'hx vm image build' into Firecracker images. Memory snapshots can start many new sandboxes. Volumes are team-scoped, persistent, multi-attach. Default 'ubuntu' sudo user. Outbound internet allowed by default; allowOut/denyOut policies. Plan concurrency caps are stated for browsers only; sandbox concurrency limits unpublished. Snapshot/volume/disk storage prices unpublished.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: 5,000 credits ($5) to test (modelled as one-time credit); no proxies/CAPTCHA; 7-day retention. Free plan must upgrade when its credits run out (no top-up on Free).

plans.name: Startup
plans.note: $30/month includes 30,000 credits ($30) - fee is spent as usage; extra credits $0.001 each. Auto CAPTCHA, basic stealth, residential proxies, 30-day retention.

plans.name: Scale
plans.note: $100/month includes 100,000 credits ($100). Premium residential proxies, 30-day retention.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: 1000+ concurrent, ultra stealth, custom proxies, asia-south, HIPAA/SOC 2, 180+ day retention, volume discounts, 14-day trial.

features.ip_note: Managed proxy network (100+ countries, IP type not stated in docs) at $10/GB, static IPs available; proxies and CAPTCHA solving need a paid plan; BYO proxy and Ultra Stealth are Enterprise-only.

extras.price: $0.001/page; $0.01/page with proxy (+$0.009); Fetch with JSON output +$0.005/page

caveats: Browser product: priced per browser-hour ($0.10) with undisclosed vCPU/RAM; not comparable to a 4 vCPU/8 GiB VM.
isolation null: session isolation technology is not documented (only 'isolated cookies, storage, cache').
Proxy bandwidth $10/GB is not modelled as egress (egress_gib null); for scraping it usually dominates the bill (100 GB = $1,000).
Free plan 5,000 credits modelled as one-time $5; pricing page says 'Credits Included' without saying monthly vs one-time.
Plan fees convert 1:1 into credits (fee_is_credit true); purchased top-up credits expire after 12 months.
Max session 12 h from API schema (timeoutMinutes max 720); default timeout is a team setting.
SOC 2 unverified (pricing page lists 'HIPAA/SOC 2' for Enterprise; security page only says 'aligned with' SOC 2 criteria).
asia-south region only on Enterprise/Select plans; europe-west assumed available on all plans (not stated otherwise).
Hyperbrowser Sandboxes are priced: $0.045/vCPU-h + $0.015/GiB-h on allocation (see new mode 'sandbox'). Snapshot, volume and disk storage prices are not published.
Overage is not automatic: once plan credits are used, usage needs manual credit purchase or opt-in auto-reload (purchased credits expire after 12 months). Plan changes are prorated and immediate.
API calls are free and paid plans have no API rate limits; Enterprise gets 'custom rate limits'.

fleet.tiers: Free 1; Startup 25; Scale 100; Enterprise 1,000+ via contact.
fleet.notes: Verified with rendered pricing page. 10 fits Startup, 50 Scale; 300/1,000 Enterprise. Monthly credit budgets and duration restrictions are additional constraints.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: When a sandbox is created, it is always running until you stop it or it times out.
snapshot_auto.note: Sandboxes have no stop/resume or hibernate: stop (or lifetime timeout) ends the sandbox; state survives only via explicit memory snapshots or mounted volumes. Browser sessions likewise end on stop/timeout; only opt-in browser Profiles persist cookies/storage (not a machine snapshot).

snapshot_on_demand.quote:
When you take a snapshot, you are freezing the sandbox's memory, processes, and filesystem at that point in time.
Starting a sandbox from a snapshot is instant and you can start a new sandbox from the same snapshot multiple times.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Sandbox product only: createMemorySnapshot on a running sandbox (POST /api/sandbox/{id}/snapshot); memory included; new sandboxes boot from it (snapshotName/snapshotId), i.e. fork/template. Not available for browser sessions.

own_agent_api.quote:
All agents share the same operational model: start a task, optionally poll for
  status, and fetch the final result.
own_agent_api.note: Browser-agent task API: HyperAgent (own), Browser Use, Claude / OpenAI CUA / Gemini / Meta / Grok / Jev computer use; start with a task prompt, poll status/steps, stop; follow-ups by passing an existing sessionId with keepBrowserOpen. These are browser agents driven by Hyperbrowser against its cloud browser, polled not streamed. For Sandboxes, claude-code / codex / openclaw base images only preinstall the CLIs; no API to prompt Claude Code/Codex inside a sandbox (only generic exec/process APIs).

harness_api.quote:
All agents share the same operational model: start a task, optionally poll for
  status, and fetch the final result.
harness_api.note: Browser-agent task API: HyperAgent (own), Browser Use, Claude / OpenAI CUA / Gemini / Meta / Grok / Jev computer use; start with a task prompt, poll status/steps, stop; follow-ups by passing an existing sessionId with keepBrowserOpen. These are browser agents driven by Hyperbrowser against its cloud browser, polled not streamed. For Sandboxes, claude-code / codex / openclaw base images only preinstall the CLIs; no API to prompt Claude Code/Codex inside a sandbox (only generic exec/process APIs).

egress_allowlist.quote:
Outbound destinations to allow. Entries can be IPv4 addresses, IPv4 CIDR
  ranges, exact domains, or wildcard domains such as `*.example.com`.
egress_allowlist.note: Sandboxes: allowInternetAccess=false for default-deny, allowOut (IPv4/CIDR/domain/wildcard), denyOut (IPv4/CIDR only); settable at create and updatable live (PUT /api/sandbox/{id}/network). Domain rules only for HTTP :80 / HTTPS :443 via Host / SNI; DNS restricted to allowed names; IPv6 targets unsupported. Not documented for browser sessions.

egress_http_rules.quote:
Domain rules apply to HTTP on port `80` and HTTPS on port `443`. HTTPS
  matching uses the TLS server name.
egress_http_rules.note: The policy schema is only allowInternetAccess / allowOut / denyOut; matching is by Host/SNI hostname, no method/path/header rules.

ingress_rules.quote: When `auth` is `true`, the exposed custom URL now requires the auth token to be passed on each request.
ingress_rules.note: Ports must be explicitly exposed (expose/unexpose API, --port N or N:auth); each exposed port is either public (auth:false) or requires the sandbox bearer token; browserUrl gives an expiring grant for browser access. Port 4001 reserved for the runtime API. No IP allowlist documented.

guest_firewall.note: Sandboxes are Firecracker VMs (custom images are 'Firecracker image' builds) and base images have 'A default `ubuntu` sudo user'; nftables/iptables not documented. Browser sessions: no shell, n/a.

secret_proxy.quote: Environment variables to inject into the process.
secret_proxy.note: No credential-injecting egress proxy documented; sandbox secrets are passed as env vars / files (e.g. OpenClaw guide puts the model key in the sandbox). Related but not a proxy: Browser Use tasks' sensitive-data map keeps real values from the LLM ('The LLM only sees placeholders (x\_user, x\_pass)... Real values are injected directly into form fields after the LLM call'), but the values do enter the browser; browser Profiles persist logins.

volume_attach.quote: Volumes are persistent, team scoped filesystems that you can attach to a sandbox at launch.
volume_attach.note: Sandbox product; mounts set at launch only ('Mounts are currently configured at sandbox launch'; updating mounts on a running sandbox is not supported); rw or ro per mount. Storage price unpublished.

volume_shared.quote: You can attach a volume to multiple sandboxes, and a volume is synced across writes.
volume_shared.note: Read-write or read-only per mount (type rw|ro); a third mode `shared` is listed as 'currently reserved'. Consistency semantics beyond 'synced across writes' not documented.
